accepted.reason: Supabase Management API reports this setting is available only on Supabase Pro plans and up for the current project.

accepted.reason: The cleanup outbox is service-role-only: PUBLIC, anon, and authenticated have no table privileges, while RLS remains enabled as defense in depth.
accepted.next_action: Keep grants service-role-only and retain storage cleanup boundary tests whenever the outbox contract changes.

accepted.reason: Invocation reconciliation is service-role-only: PUBLIC, anon, and authenticated have no table privileges, while RLS remains enabled as defense in depth.
accepted.next_action: Keep grants service-role-only and retain invocation lifecycle tests whenever reconciliation changes.

accepted.reason: The invalid-identity quarantine is in the unexposed private schema and staging proves anon, authenticated, and service_role have no direct DML privileges; privileged maintenance functions own the boundary.
accepted.next_action: Keep the private-schema placement, zero browser-role grants, and quarantine integrity checks as release gates.

accepted.reason: The current-publication pointer is an unexposed private table with no direct browser-role DML privileges; public access is only through bounded projection RPCs.
accepted.next_action: Retain zero direct grants and the exact-publication projection tests whenever publication switching changes.

accepted.reason: Publication metadata is stored in the unexposed private schema with no direct browser-role DML privileges and is exposed only through a fixed public projection.

accepted.reason: Materialized listing versions are isolated in the unexposed private schema with no direct browser-role DML privileges; only allowlisted public fields leave through bounded RPCs.
accepted.next_action: Retain zero direct grants and the raw-table denial plus public-projection staging tests.

review.reason: Unused-index advisories require production query telemetry before dropping indexes; blind removal can slow listing, search, admin, and analytics paths.
review.next_action: Compare against pg_stat_user_indexes, pg_stat_statements, slow-query logs, and recent release history before dropping each index.

review.reason: Policy consolidation is performance work but can change RLS semantics; each table/action needs an RLS regression test before changing policies.
review.next_action: Group duplicate permissive policies by table/action, consolidate only when RLS tests prove identical user-visible access.

review.reason: Public listing cards require display name, avatar, and a coarse agent/seller label. The stable RPC accepts only user IDs and returns only those explicitly public fields without exposing account roles, billing state, or tenant membership.
review.next_action: Keep RPC output and execute grants covered by public API and RLS tests; replace it with an equally narrow public projection if Supabase adds a safer native role-aware view pattern.

review.reason: Authenticated listing cards consume the same constrained public profile projection as anonymous cards. The RPC does not return plan, pricing, billing, organization, or authoritative role data.
review.next_action: Keep RPC output and execute grants covered by public API and RLS tests; remove browser execution if card enrichment moves behind a service boundary.

review.reason: The public directory function returns a fixed allowlist of marketplace fields and excludes moderation, calendar, and internal notes while raw professional rows remain owner/admin-only.
review.next_action: Keep the output allowlist, raw-table denial policy, and invoker-view regression tests as hard release gates.

review.reason: Authenticated directory readers use the same constrained public projection without receiving raw professional moderation or calendar fields.
review.next_action: Keep the output allowlist, raw-table denial policy, and invoker-view regression tests as hard release gates.

review.reason: Anonymous catalogue traffic needs the fixed active/non-off-market projection. The no-argument RPC returns only the allowlisted public view row type and retains no raw-table grants.
review.next_action: Keep the output allowlist, anonymous denial tests for raw tables, and public API projection tests as hard release gates.

review.reason: Signed-in catalogue traffic uses the same allowlisted public projection as anonymous users; the RPC does not expose tenancy, cadastral, billing, or internal workflow fields.
review.next_action: Keep the output allowlist and raw-table denial matrix covered by staging RLS tests.

review.reason: Owner, organization and platform-admin screens require full listing records, while the RPC view predicate checks auth.uid(), ownership, listing:view organization permission, or authoritative platform administration before returning rows.
review.next_action: Keep owner, organization-member, outsider and administrator read tests as hard staging gates; never grant this RPC to anon.

review.reason: Public relationship surfaces need a minimal listing identity projection for active listings. The RPC returns only route/card reference fields and applies the fixed public-or-caller-related predicate.
review.next_action: Keep the reference-field allowlist and anonymous inactive-listing denial tests as hard gates.

review.reason: Authenticated favorites, conversations, viewings, contacts, leads and project screens need minimal listing references without receiving raw listing-table access.
review.next_action: Keep each relationship predicate covered by role/action regression tests and retain the minimal return type.

review.reason: The legacy capacity RPC remains authenticated for compatibility while edge-facing capacity flows use the user-scoped service RPCs.
review.next_action: Remove authenticated access after all clients and smoke tests prove only open-house Edge Functions call capacity helpers.

review.reason: Agent data-input submission is an authenticated RPC with role, ban, quota, and idempotency checks enforced inside the function.
review.next_action: Keep denial-path tests current and migrate browser submission to an Edge Function if additional moderation steps are added.

review.reason: The public auction projection reads only a fixed materialized-publication snapshot and allowlisted auction fields while raw snapshot and auction tables remain inaccessible to browser roles.
review.next_action: Keep publication identity, bounded listing IDs, output allowlists, and raw-table denial covered by staging catalogue tests.

review.reason: Homepage reads are served from an immutable public snapshot and return only the fixed homepage aggregate instead of exposing private snapshot tables.
review.next_action: Keep the response contract, publication identity, and anonymous raw-table denial tests as hard staging gates.

review.reason: Exact listing reads use the immutable public snapshot and return only an allowlisted public listing envelope for one bounded identifier.
review.next_action: Keep inactive/off-market denial, output allowlist, and exact-publication tests as hard staging gates.

review.reason: The publication RPC exposes only the current immutable publication identity required to bind subsequent public reads and never exposes the private control table.
review.next_action: Keep the fixed return shape and raw-table denial proof tied to every catalogue publication change.

review.reason: Search queries are bounded, filter-normalized reads over the immutable public snapshot and return only the public listing projection; private snapshot tables have no browser grants.
review.next_action: Keep filter bounds, cursor validation, output allowlists, and raw-table denial in the staging performance/security suite.

review.reason: The public envelope is a bounded read-only auction projection that excludes invalid, duplicate, and private quarantine rows while keeping source tables inaccessible.
review.next_action: Keep limit/filter bounds, invalid-identity exclusion, and output-field tests as release gates.

review.reason: The visible-candidate RPC is a bounded read-only compatibility projection with explicit visibility and quarantine exclusions; raw auction data remains inaccessible to browser roles.
review.next_action: Keep visibility, quarantine, and bounded-result regression tests until all clients use the envelope RPC.

review.reason: Authenticated promotion activation enforces the caller principal, listing ownership, entitlement balance, idempotency, and promotion type inside the RPC.
review.next_action: Keep owner/outsider, balance, concurrency, and idempotency tests as hard release gates.

review.reason: Authenticated promotion deactivation verifies the caller owns the target listing before changing its active promotion state.
review.next_action: Keep owner/outsider and entitlement-state tests tied to this RPC.

review.reason: Realtime and TURN authorization require an authenticated SECURITY DEFINER predicate that validates the room topic and current user participation without exposing room membership rows.
review.next_action: Keep malformed-topic, participant, outsider, and realtime-policy tests as hard release gates.

review.reason: The authenticated quota RPC derives the caller from auth.uid() and returns only the caller's effective visible-auction limit without exposing subscription records.
review.next_action: Keep anonymous denial and role/plan quota matrix tests tied to this RPC.

review.reason: The authenticated management catalogue derives the caller principal and returns only listings the owner, permitted organization member, or platform administrator may manage.
review.next_action: Keep owner, organization-member, outsider, pagination, and platform-admin tests as hard release gates.

review.reason: The management summary applies the same caller-scoped owner, organization, and administrator predicate and returns only aggregate counts for that authorized set.
review.next_action: Keep summary parity and outsider-denial tests aligned with the management catalogue predicate.

review.reason: Upload registration verifies the authenticated project owner, bucket, normalized object path, and lifecycle state before recording cleanup ownership.
review.next_action: Keep owner/outsider, bucket/path, state-transition, and cleanup lifecycle tests as hard release gates.

review.reason: Realtime video-room policies intentionally inspect JWT claims and room topics to enforce participant-only channels; prior migrations wrapped claim reads where practical.
review.next_action: Profile realtime policy latency and simplify channel authorization only if it preserves viewing and consultation isolation.

review.reason: Listing inserts must call the quota guard for free/pro plan enforcement; the policy uses a cached auth.uid() and a race-resistant helper.
review.next_action: Monitor insert latency and keep quota-denial regression tests tied to buyer/seller/agent/developer limits.
